clue.text: I'm so sexy in new lace undergarment

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside the other set
sexy suggests being worked up and tumbled about, so the preceding words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged to wrap round the other part

indicators.note: new signals that the following word is remade into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admires how alluring they look in a new piece of lace lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sexy' looks like a description of the wearer, but it shuffles the words before it, while 'new' does the same to the word after; one result then sits inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light, sleeveless top worn under clothing, an item of women's underwear.

clue.text: Keep left in station

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for station

parts.note: station in the sense of social rank or class
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay on the left while at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb; it is the noun, the fortified tower of a castle, and 'station' means rank, not a railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest central tower of a fortress, so by extension it stands for the whole stronghold.

clue.text: New, in fish sauce

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for the fish

parts.note: a moray is a type of eel
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fresh twist on a sauce served with fish, which is exactly where mornay often appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Mornay is a cheese-flavoured white sauce, often served with fish or eggs.

clue.text: Czar's aunt, originally from a Bolivian city

indicators.note: originally hints that the letters were once in a different arrangement, so they must be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler's aunt turns out to have come from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' seems to belong with 'from', describing birthplace; it is the signal to reorder the letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Cruz de la Sierra is the largest city in Bolivia.

clue.text: Sweet woman, crossing warden

parts.note: a lollipop is a sweet on a stick
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A kind woman who helps people across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lollipop lady is a school crossing patrol, named for the round sign on a pole she holds up to stop traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday British name for a woman who stops traffic so children can cross safely near a school.

clue.text: A couple of lines in poor song

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the word for poor

parts.note: poor in quality means bad
taken as written
L stands for line, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A criticism of a weak song, judged on a few of its lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, usually slow and sentimental or telling a story in verse.

clue.text: Change flag when heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the front letter is removed

parts.note: to flag is to tire or falter

explanation.surface: Advice to swap a banner as you set out somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but here it is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change or modify it.

clue.text: Cause of one leering lasciviously?

indicators.note: lasciviously suggests wanton, unruly behaviour, so the letters before it get jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: What might make a man ogle?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and within it 'one' and 'leering' together are rearranged; the question mark flags the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, often worn to look alluring, so it could well prompt an ogle.

clue.text: Put on, before season, an equestrian event

parts.note: to put on clothes is to dress
to season timber or cheese is to age it

explanation.surface: Getting dressed before the start of a season of horse shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a time of year; here it is the verb meaning to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competitive discipline in which a horse performs precise trained movements.

clue.text: Beginning to laugh, interrupting funny gag

indicators.note: interrupting puts that letter into the middle of another word

parts.note: funny in the sense of odd

indicators.note: beginning to picks out just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of laugh

explanation.surface: Someone starts giggling in the middle of a comic joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny gag' reads as a joke; 'gag' is the verb meaning to choke, and 'funny' supplies the word for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to choke or stifle them, close in sense to throttling.

clue.text: Article by good man on church's position

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written by a virtuous man about where the church stands on an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in the order 'by' and 'on' put them: the saint, then the article, with the church at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or attitude taken on an issue, as well as a physical posture.

clue.text: All given lift after morality play

parts.note: Everyman is a famous late-medieval English morality play
to jack up is to lift, and a jack is a lifting device

explanation.surface: Everyone was cheered up after watching a medieval moral drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the order: the lifting word comes after the play's title. A nod to the setter's own pen-name.
explanation.definitionFit: Every man jack is an idiom meaning every single person, everybody without exception.

clue.text: Buddhist monk holding head of lowing animal

indicators.note: holding means the monk's title wraps round the selected letter

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

indicators.note: head of takes only the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of lowing

explanation.surface: A monk in charge of a mooing farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American camelid kept for wool and as a pack animal.

clue.text: Popular French novelist's crossing small British city

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: crossing means one word stretches across another, holding it

parts.note: Jules Verne, the French novelist, with the possessive S
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A well-loved French writer journeys across a small British city.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra S goes in just before the possessive S, so the novelist's name with its 's spans the small letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is a city in the Scottish Highlands, so it is a British city.

clue.text: Checking text from academic going round old English university

indicators.note: going round means the academic's title surrounds the next letter

parts.note: short for professor
O is the abbreviation for old
the University of Reading, in the English town of Reading

explanation.surface: A professor at an old English university examining a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town west of London with its own university, so 'English university' supplies the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is the careful reading of written copy to find and correct errors before publication.

clue.text: An Italian city, southern state capital

parts.note: taken as written
Napoli is the Italian name for Naples
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A southern Italian city serving as a regional capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Naples does lie in southern Italy, which disguises that 'southern' only supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapolis is the capital of the US state of Maryland.

clue.text: Liking page's charm

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
to charm is to enchant

explanation.surface: Enjoying the appeal of a young servant boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or fondness for something, a liking.

clue.text: Rough sailor varies manoeuvres

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: manoeuvres are deliberate movements, so the preceding word's letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough seaman keeps changing the way he steers his ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive is rough or harsh, whether a scouring surface or a grating manner.

clue.text: Speculation after son's dismissed? His crime?

definitions.text: Speculation after son's dismissed? His crime?

parts.note: surface reading: a son is sacked and people start to gossip about why
setter's reading: drop the S for son from speculation and the remaining word is a legal term for misappropriating funds, perhaps why he was dismissed

explanation.surface: A son has been fired and everyone wonders what offence he committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from SPECULATION leaves PECULATION, the formal word for stealing funds in your care, which the answer is a synonym of.
explanation.definitionFit: Embezzlement is the theft of money entrusted to one's care, exactly what peculation means.

clue.text: A soldier entering a function slowly

indicators.note: entering means the first pieces go inside the later ones

parts.note: the second a in the clue, taken as written
a do is a party or social function
taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier walks into a reception at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical tempo marking meaning slowly and at ease.

clue.text: Gay bishop set on fire by male

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
something set on fire has been lit
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A clergyman has his house set alight by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its older sense of carefree and cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means happy and carefree, the traditional meaning of gay.

clue.text: Typeface used by Cambridge college lecturer penning first of novels

indicators.note: penning means writing in, so the lecturer encloses that letter

parts.note: Clare is one of the colleges of Cambridge University

indicators.note: first of takes only the initial letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of novels
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A Cambridge academic chooses a font for writing novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarendon is a bold slab-serif typeface, a name for a style of printed lettering.

clue.text: Close to campsite, put down an antelope

indicators.note: close to means the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of campsite
to land an aircraft is to put it down

explanation.surface: An antelope was put down near a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests killing an animal; it means landing.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Ring about daughter's cycle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ringing word goes around the next letter

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A call to someone regarding the daughter's bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' reads as a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to turn a bicycle's cranks with your feet, which is to cycle.

clue.text: Beast kept by Pakistani male

indicators.note: kept by means the letters are held within the words that follow

parts.note: found straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A wild creature owned by a man from Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any animal, especially a large or wild one.

clue.text: A name in staircase window

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the word for staircase

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone's name is etched into a window on the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a small semicircular window above a door, often fan-shaped.

clue.text: Hear about object, all the rage

indicators.note: about means going around, so the hearing word encloses the word for object

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
an end is an object or aim

explanation.surface: Listen to talk about something that is the latest craze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the judge's word, as in hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, the latest thing, which is what all the rage means.

clue.text: On which runners make tracks?

parts.note: surface reading: an athletics track where sprinters race
setter's reading: runners are the long blades of skis, which leave tracks in snow on a downhill course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make tracks' sounds like the idiom for leaving in a hurry, and 'runners' like athletes; both are literal snow sports here.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski slope is a snowy hillside prepared for skiing, where skis cut grooves in the snow.
